questions.q: What programming structure is the Conditional Split transformation's behavior most similar to?
options: A CASE decision structure
A try/catch error handler
A FOR loop
A recursive function call
questions.explain: Microsoft's own documentation describes the Conditional Split transformation as similar to a CASE decision structure — it evaluates expressions in order and routes each row to the first matching output.

questions.q: In a Conditional Split with multiple conditions, which output does a row go to?
options: Whichever output happens to run fastest
The default output, always, regardless of the conditions
Every output whose condition evaluates to true
The output for the first condition, in listed order, that evaluates to true
questions.explain: Order is significant: the transformation checks conditions top to bottom and sends the row to the output for the first one that evaluates true, ignoring the rest.

questions.q: What happens to a row that doesn't match any of the defined conditions in a Conditional Split?
options: It causes the package to fail immediately
It's dropped from the data flow silently
It's routed to the required default output
It gets sent to every output at once
questions.explain: A Conditional Split transformation requires a default output, so any row that matches no condition still has somewhere defined to go.

questions.q: If you need to evaluate several conditions independently — not just the first match — for the same row, what should you do?
options: Reverse the order of the existing conditions
Chain multiple Conditional Split transformations in sequence
Use a Lookup transformation instead
Increase the number of default outputs
questions.explain: A single Conditional Split only ever sends a row to one output — the first matching case. Evaluating several conditions independently requires concatenating multiple Conditional Split transformations.

questions.q: What language are Conditional Split conditions written in?
options: Regular expressions only
C# script blocks
T-SQL
Integration Services (SSIS) Expressions
questions.explain: Conditions are boolean expressions written in the SSIS expression language, built from columns, variables, functions, and operators — the same language formalized in the Expressions lesson.
